case_title.quote: NANDA GOPALAN v. STATE OF KERALA
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant stands convicted under Sections 324 and 326
number_of_accused.reason: Only one appellant is convicted and sentenced, consistent with the value of 1.

accused_gender.quote: The appellant is son of cousin of injured Sukumaran (PW1)
accused_gender.reason: Describing the appellant as a son supports male gender, though not stated outright.

accused_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the accused.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_gender.quote: He was admitted to a Medical Trust Hospital
victim_gender.reason: The injured PW-1 is referred to as male throughout.

victim_age.reason: No age is given for the victim anywhere in the judgment.

victim_caste.reason: Victim caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The appellant is son of cousin of injured Sukumaran (PW1)
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Close relative relationship is supported by the cousin's son description.

offence_category.quote: Penal Code, 1860: ss.324 and 326 - ... caused injuries
offence_category.reason: Sections 324 and 326 concern voluntarily causing hurt, so hurt is accurate.

statutory_provisions.quote: convicted under Sections 324 and 326 of the Indian Penal Code
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 324 and 326 IPC are the provisions applied.

weapon.quote: attacked PW 1 by using a bat made of coconut leaf stem
weapon.reason: Both the bat and the stone are identified as weapons.

evidence_type.correct_value: Medical evidence, witness testimony (injured, family, independent witnesses), and documents
evidence_type.quote: In addition, medical evidence and relevant documents were also produced.
evidence_type.reason: Medical and eyewitness evidence are supported; 'circumstantial' is not mentioned in the judgment.

confession.reason: The judgment does not mention any confession, so 'None' is not backed by the text.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: The judgment identifies no aggravating circumstances, so 'None noted' is consistent.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: particularly when they are close relatives, reduction in sentence can be ordered
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Compromise and close relationship are identified as mitigating factors.

trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years and three years respectively and to pay fine of Rs.30,000/-
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court conviction, sentences and Rs.30,000 compensation.

high_court_outcome.quote: which has been affirmed by the High Court with reduction in sentence
high_court_outcome.reason: The High Court affirmed the conviction with reduced sentence, as stated.

final_outcome.quote: we do no find any ground to interfere with the conviction of the appellant
final_outcome.reason: Conviction upheld while sentence reduced, so 'convicted' is accurate.

offence_finally_established.quote: the nature of weapon used does not fall under Sections 324 and 326
offence_finally_established.reason: The Court upheld the findings that the charges under Sections 324 and 326 stand.

imprisonment_type.quote: sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years and three years respectively
imprisonment_type.reason: Fixed-term rigorous imprisonment is the sentence type stated.

imprisonment_years.correct_value: Two years (s.324) and three years (s.326) originally, reduced to period already undergone
imprisonment_years.quote: rigorous imprisonment for two years and three years respectively
imprisonment_years.reason: Value 2.0 captures only the s.324 term and omits the three-year s.326 term and final reduction.

fine_rs.correct_value: Compensation of Rs.2,00,000 (increased from Rs.30,000); not a fine
fine_rs.quote: the amount of compensation is increased to Rs.2 lakhs to be paid to the victim
fine_rs.reason: Rs.2 lakh amount is correct but it is compensation, not a fine.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Accused attacked victim with coconut-leaf bat, then sat on chest and injured him with a stone; trial court convicted; High Court affirmed with reduced sentence; compromise reached during appeal.
neutral_facts.quote: leading to a reduction in the sentence and an increase in compensation
neutral_facts.reason: Reveals the Supreme Court outcome; also calls the injuries 'grievous' though this judgment does not so find for this case.

offence_severity.reason: Punishment ranges for ss.324 and 326 are not stated in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: caused injuries with a stone. PW 1 became unconscious.
attempt_completion.reason: Hurt was actually caused, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.quote: (1) 4 x 1 ems through and through lacerated wound over left angle of the mouth
physical_harm.reason: Lacerations, missing teeth, contusions and unconsciousness are all reported.

number_of_offences.reason: Two offences were charged and both were upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or financial loss is discussed beyond compensation, so 'Not applicable' fits.

premeditation_planning.reason: The judgment says nothing about premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: No motive is identified in the judgment.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Trial court held the prosecution case proved; the Supreme Court found no ground to interfere with the conviction.
key_evidence_accepted.quote: The trial court held the case of the prosecution to have been proved
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Facts are right, but the attribution to the Supreme Court accepting the version is not what the judgment states.

witness_credibility.reason: The judgment lists witnesses but makes no express credibility assessment.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Post-offence conduct is not mentioned in the judgment.

custody_duration.quote: reduced to the period already undergone
custody_duration.reason: The judgment refers to time already served but never states its duration.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: Offence date, High Court date and Supreme Court date match; trial judgment date is not stated.

legal_representation.quote: Ram Jethmalani (AC), Karan Kalia ... for the Appellant. Jogy Scaria ... for the Respondent.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names and sides match the judgment's appearance list.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR recorded by PW-2, investigation conducted, appellant sent up for trial
investigation_status.quote: PW 2 recorded the First Information Report and conducted investigation and sent up the appellant for trial.
investigation_status.reason: Charge sheet filing is not mentioned; the judgment says the appellant was sent up for trial.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural irregularity is noted in the judgment.

appeal_history.quote: reduce the sentence of imprisonment of the appellant to the period already undergone
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court steps are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution case: appellant hit PW-1 with a coconut-leaf stem bat, sat on his chest, and injured him with a stone.
prosecution_argument.quote: the appellant attacked PW 1 by using a bat made of coconut leaf stem
prosecution_argument.reason: Core facts are right, but 'grievous injuries' is not stated in the prosecution case description.

defence_argument.correct_value: Amicus curiae argued in the Supreme Court that the weapon was not dangerous and that the charge could be altered to ss.323 and 325; compromise was relied on.
defence_argument.quote: since the weapon used in the present case was not of the nature specified under Sections 324 and 326, the charge could be altered to Sections 323 and 325
defence_argument.reason: The weapon argument was made by amicus in the Supreme Court and was not raised in the lower courts.

legal_principle_applied.quote: just and appropriate sentence has to be imposed keeping in mind the proportion between crime and punishment
legal_principle_applied.reason: Proportionality principle and the factors listed match the judgment.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Relied on: Dasan (2014) 12 SCC 666; Mathai (2005) 3 SCC 260; Anwarul Haq (2005) 10 SCC 581; Ghanshyam (2003) 8 SCC 13; Bankat (2005) 1 SCC 343. Referred to: Regina v. Bibi.
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Regina vs. Bibi 1980 (1) WLR 1193 - referred to.
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All cases are listed, but Regina v. Bibi was only referred to, not relied on.

sentencing_rationale.quote: In view of the above, we are inclined to reduce the sentence
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale based on compromise and sentencing proportionality matches the judgment.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: particularly when they are close relatives, reduction in sentence can be ordered
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The Court expressly treated the compromise between close relatives as a ground for reduction.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The judgment identifies no aggravating factors, consistent with 'None'.

other_sentence_order.quote: increasing the amount of compensation to Rs.2 lakhs to be paid to the victim within three months, failing which the sentence awarded by the High Court will stand affirmed
other_sentence_order.reason: Compensation increase, three-month deadline and default condition are all stated.
